scripts.comment: This program makes spokes radiating out from an inner circle.
The spokes created in the program above are not radiating at a right angle to the circle. How would you get the spokes to radiate at a right angle?
The following two examples code one section of the circle and a spoke. Compare the two codes.

Example #2 Turn 90 degrees from the circle. Make the spoke by moving forward. Turn around 180 degrees (so you face the opposite way). Move forward to return to the circle. In this example, the turtle ends up pointing toward the center of the circle.

The difference between these two methods: In Example 1, the turtle finishes pointing away from the center. In Example 2, the turtle finishes pointing toward the center. Both ways are correct—you can choose whichever works best for your design.

This program makes spokes radiating out from an inner circle. First, part of a circle is drawn. Then, the turtle moves away from the circle by moving forward a certain number of steps (positive steps). After that, it returns to the same point by moving backward (negative steps). This routine repeats 12 times, because: 360 degrees / 30 degrees = 12 In the example above, the spokes are not at a right angle to the circle.

Example #1 Turn 90 degrees from the circle. Make the spoke by moving forward. Return back by moving the same number of steps backward (negative steps). In this example, when you are done, the turtle is pointing away from the center of the circle.
Example #1 needs a turn left 90 degrees to orient the turtle in the correct direction to make the next spoke.
Example #2 needs a turn right 90 degrees to orient the turtle in the correct direction to make the next spoke..

How can you vary the number of spokes? You can make it variable by creating a variable called “number of spokes.” Steps to do this: Go to the Variables block and click “Make a Variable.” Name the variable “number of spokes.” Use this variable in your code instead of a fixed number. To find out how much the turtle should turn after each spoke, you divide 360 by the number of spokes: Formula: Degrees to turn = 360 ÷ number of spokes Example: If number of spokes = 12, then 360 ÷ 12 = 30 degrees. The turtle will turn 30 degrees after each spoke.
How do you change the length of the spokes? It can be variablized by making a variable called "length of spokes".
Example #2 uses a random length for all to the spokes. Each time the code is run, a value between 0 and 200 will be chosen.

Example #3 - uses a random length for each spoke. The set block for "length of spokes" was moved into the repeat for each spoke. Each time a spoke is made, the length will be varied, creating an interesting design.
How do you change the angle of each spoke radiating from the circle? It can be variablized by making a variable called "angle of spokes".

When you draw the spoke, you: Turn by the spoke angle (so the spoke is pointed the right way). Move forward to draw the spoke line. When you are done with the spoke and need to get back to the circle and get ready for the next spoke, you must: Turn around to face the starting point. But you don’t always turn a full 180 degrees—you use this calculation: 180 degrees - angle of spokes Why do you subtract the spoke angle from 180? Because the first turn angled you away from the circle. Subtracting the spoke angle makes the turtle face exactly back along the spoke path.
